sources.entry: Buddy - Study helper in the notch that explains what is on your screen out loud while drawing on it. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/projects-hacks/buddy)

summary.one_liner: Buddy is a macOS study and screen-help app that lives in the notch, answers questions about what is on your screen out loud, and draws on the screen while it talks.
summary.what_it_does: Buddy is invoked by holding Control + Option to ask by voice, or Control + Option + T to type a question. It captures the screen, answers out loud, and draws on the screen while speaking, using a model chosen per question from Claude Sonnet, Opus, or Gemini Argon. It can explain code, papers, dashboards, and lecture videos, give hints on LeetCode before answers, and walk through an app one step at a time while waiting for the user to click. When a terminal or editor shows an error, the notch glows and Buddy can explain the line that caused it. It can teach a topic on a whiteboard and check the user's explanation back, and it can review diagrams in Excalidraw, draw.io, Miro, or Freeform. Lessons are saved as local notebook pages, and a map shows which ideas are fading. The README states that analytics are none and that notebook data is kept on the Mac.
use_cases: get explanations of code, papers, or dashboards on screen
learn a new topic with a spoken and drawn walkthrough
get step-by-step help using an unfamiliar Mac app
understand an error in a terminal or editor
review and critique a diagram or design in Excalidraw, draw.io, Miro, or Freeform
how_to_run: Alternatively, download the app; macOS asks for Open Anyway once because Buddy is not notarized, then setup asks for name and API keys
Building from source: needs Xcode 16 and a self-signed code signing certificate named 'Clicky Local Dev'
git clone the repo, cd buddy, then run: zsh scripts/build-local.sh
stack: Swift (macOS app, inferred from Xcode requirement)
notable: Answers are spoken while the drawing is still being generated, sentence by sentence
Teach-back mode: explain a topic to Buddy and it marks gaps in red on the board
Screen content and voice processing are largely done on the Mac; notebook pages are stored locally
Error detection watches the front window of terminals, editors, and coding judges
caveats: Not notarized, so macOS requires a manual Open Anyway step on first launch
Requires API keys and paid model usage; each question costs roughly one to six cents per the README
Building from source requires a self-signed certificate with a legacy name, 'Clicky Local Dev'
Requires macOS with a notch-related interface; the README does not state minimum macOS version
Some features (lecture audio capture, system audio) need extra permissions the user must grant
